messages:
elaine: Quick share — I ran an SLA simulation for air-gapped/offline clusters that have two fallback modes: 
  1) fallback-to-hosted (forward requests to hosted inference)
  2) degraded-local-mode (trim models, evict KV caches, serve reduced feature set locally)
  TL;DR: fallback-to-hosted reduces error budget burn but increases p99 latency; degraded-local-mode keeps latency lower but increases operational risk and cost.

oliver: Can you drop the assumptions and the numbers you saw?

elaine: Sure — sim assumptions: 50 clusters, avg 500 RPS per cluster during incident window, request mix heavy on chat/generation, simulated storage pressure events causing model evictions.
  Results (approx):
  - fallback-to-hosted: successful served fraction ~92%, p50 160ms, p95 420ms, p99 890ms, error-rate ~0.6% (network/retry fallout).
  - degraded-local-mode: successful served fraction ~88%, p50 70ms, p95 160ms, p99 300ms, error-rate ~1.8% (OOM-triggered retries + partial feature errors).
  - operator interventions: ~1 intervention/30d for degraded-local-mode vs 1/90d for fallback-to-hosted (because of cache/state reconciliation).

sam: From cost POV how big is hosted bump?

elaine: In our sim, traffic forwarded to hosted added ~+18% token bill for affected customers during the window. If we had aggressive batching + caching at gateway we could reduce that to ~+7%. Also hidden ops cost higher for degraded-local-mode (investigation, debug time).

maria: Security/compliance angle: token forwarding means we need ephemeral credentials + KMS + audit logs. Any PII redaction in-flight?

elaine: We simulated token-forwarding with ephemeral short-lived keys and an audit sink. Works technically, but legal flagged that some customers will require explicit opt-in. Alternative is a model-proxy that strips sensitive fields before forwarding — bigger perf hit (~+150ms median).

deploy-bot: simulation-job 1775556666 completed — artifacts: https://ci.internal/sims/1775556666 :thumbsup:

oliver: Proposed fallback policy for the RFC: default to degraded-local-mode for the first 5m of an incident (preserve latency), then escalate to fallback-to-hosted if backpressure persists > 5m or error budget burn > 0.5%. Add an opt-in flag per-customer for token-forwarding and a separate redaction-proxy path.

elaine: Sounds reasonable. I'll draft the RFC with the simulation data and two concrete operator playbooks (degraded-first and hosted-first). I'll include the rollout gating metrics and the small config snippet for policy: 

  ```json
  {
    "fallback_policy": "degraded-first",
    "degraded_window_seconds": 300,
    "hosted_escalation_thresholds": {"error_budget_pct": 0.5, "backpressure_pct": 20}
  }
  ```

sam: I can implement the gating flags + metric hooks next sprint (estimate ~2 dev-weeks).

maria: I'll loop legal on opt-in wording and track any compliance redlines.

elaine: I'll post an RFC draft by EOD Tue and link the sim artifacts. Thanks all.
